**Question:** When a FILE argument names something that exists but is not a readable text file — a directory, for instance — should that count as an unreadable file? (FR-025)

**Why it matters:** The Assumptions section puts "directory arguments" out of scope, which could be read as "undefined behaviour". If it is undefined, someone running the tool on a directory by mistake could get a crash with a stack trace instead of a clear message, and no test would be written for it.

**Recommended:** Option A — out of scope should mean "we don't recurse into it", not "we behave unpredictably"; routing it through the existing FR-025 error path gives a clear diagnostic and exit 2 with no new machinery, which is exactly what Constitution principle II asks for.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Yes — a directory or any other argument that cannot be opened and read as text takes the FR-025 path: a diagnostic naming it, processing stops, exit status 2 |
| B | No — skip a directory with a warning and continue with the remaining files, exit 0 |
| C | Leave it genuinely undefined; whatever the runtime does is acceptable |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
